title: Integrated Sobolev pairings, compatible local distributions and Hilbert completions
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a smooth real $m$-manifold [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold] and $B\to N$ a smooth rank-$r$ real vector bundle [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle] with positive definite fibre inner products; use its smooth sections [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections]. Use the metric volume $\mu$, finite smooth localization $P$, measurable a.e. classes $L^2(B,\mu)$, coordinate multi-partials and weak Sobolev subsets of [def-sfb-bundle-sobolev-space], without introducing another such space or localization. For actual sections define $q_0(u,v)=\int_N\langle u,v\rangle\,d\mu$. Define $q_{s,P}(u,v)=\sum_{i,k}\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\int_{\mathbf R^m}\partial^\alpha w_{ik}(u)\,\partial^\alpha w_{ik}(v)\,dy$, where $w_{ik}$ uses exactly the chart, frame and cutoff of $P$, extended by zero, and includes the zero multi-index. On the shared $L^2$ classes use $q_0$ on representatives for their integrated pairing. For a smooth chart $c:U\to V$ and smooth bundle frame $e$ on $W$, local coefficient tests are the $\mathbf R^r$-valued compactly supported smooth tests [def-sfb-local-coefficient-tests] on $V\cap c^{-1}(W)$, where $c^{-1}:V\to U$ denotes the inverse chart. Pair an $L^2$ class with such a test by integrating its frame coefficients against the test over coordinate Lebesgue measure. Relative to metric volume, the intrinsic test density is $v\mapsto\langle e_x(v),\phi(c(x))\rangle/\sqrt{\det G_c(c(x))}$ on $U\cap W$, extended by zero; $G_c$ is the shared chart Gram matrix. A family of local coefficient functionals is a distribution if each is continuous real-linear on its test space and every finite sum of tests defining the zero intrinsic dual-bundle density gives sum of pairings zero; this is the usual density and change-of-frame compatibility. A Hilbert completion of a real pairing $q$ on a real vector space $S$ is a complete real inner product space $H$ and a dense real-linear map $a:S\to H$ satisfying $\langle a(u),a(v)\rangle=q(u,v)$. Its real scalar action is the one inherited from the inner product space, not an additional independently chosen module structure. Injectivity, existence and the analytic realizations are asserted by the Sobolev realization theorem, not built into these data.
